deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to the drafts for Riemann's Inaugural Dissertation (1851), 'Grundlagen fuer eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veraenderlichen complexen Groesse', Arts. 9-11. The previous page (28r) proves the following. If u and u' satisfy Delta u = Delta u' = 0 in a surface T, then the boundary integral of (u' du/dp - u du'/dp) ds keeps its value under any deformation or enlargement of the domain, as long as the discontinuities are still enclosed. Taking u' = log r, this gives Gauss's mean-value formula: u(centre) = (1/2pi) * integral over phi from 0 to 2pi of u(centre + r e^{i phi}) d phi. That formula is the tool used on this page. The page states and proves two of the numbered Lehrsaetze for functions with Delta u = 0 on T. The upper half is heavily crossed out and only partly legible.

(a) Upper block: end of Satz II and its proof. Reconstructed claim: u cannot equal a constant a on a part A of T without being constant on all of T.
- Proof sketch as far as legible. Suppose u = a on a part A, and u is greater than a 'in einem entgegengesetzten Theile B'.
- Then one can choose a circle whose centre ('Mittelpunkt') lies in A. Part of its circumference lies in A, where u = a. The rest lies in B, where u > a.
- The mean of u over the circle would then exceed a. But the mean must equal u(centre) = a. Contradiction.
- The word 'Mittelpunkt' and the fragments 'Theile in A ... B ... u_1 - u_2 ... den Theil derselben' fit this reading.
- Then: 'Auf ganz aehnliche Weise ... u nicht in einem ... kleineren Werth a haben koennen ...'. That is, by the same argument u cannot have at an interior point a value a that is smaller (or larger) than all values in a surrounding region. This is the strong minimum/maximum principle, again from the mean-value property: if u(P) = a < u on a punctured disc around P, the circle mean would exceed a.

(b) Lower block: Satz III, the identity theorem / unique continuation for harmonic functions. Statement: 'Wenn die Function u in einem Theile von T gegeben ist, so ist sie dadurch fuer den uebrigen Theil dieser Flaeche [nicht] willkuerlich', i.e. it is determined there.
- Proof. Let u_1 and u_2 be two functions satisfying the conditions; consider the difference u_1 - u_2.
- Suppose u_2 = u_1 everywhere on a part A of T, but u_2 differs from u_1 in the remaining part.
- Then u_1 - u_2 would be harmonic (by linearity; this step is implicit, mine). It would be = 0 throughout A and not = 0 elsewhere.
- This contradicts Satz II applied to u_1 - u_2 with a = 0. QED.

(c) Pencil scratch (vertical and oblique). It runs through the middle and right margin, in a lighter hand. Fragments look like exponential expressions, e.g. e^{-x...}, x+iy and second-derivative terms. They are not legible enough to reconstruct, and they do not belong to the proof text.
errors: No mathematical error is visible in the legible argument.
Implicit step: Satz III needs u_1 - u_2 to be harmonic again, which holds by linearity of Laplace's equation. Riemann does not state this.
Implicit step: Satz III needs the remaining part of T to be connected to A. In the dissertation, connectedness of T is assumed.

Implicit step: the circle argument needs a disc lying entirely in T and centred in A whose boundary meets the region where u differs from a. Choosing a centre near the boundary of A guarantees this; this is not spelled out.

The draft only treats the case u > a in B. The general case (u different from a, possibly of both signs) needs the max/min principle or a connectedness argument. The final dissertation handles this more carefully.

results.what: A harmonic function constant on an open subregion is constant everywhere (proof via the circle mean value).
results.modern_name: Mean-value property and identity/rigidity of harmonic functions
results.usually_credited_to: Mean value: Gauss (1840, Allgemeine Lehrsaetze); the statement as used here: Riemann, Dissertation 1851, Art. 11

results.what: u cannot attain at an interior point a value smaller (larger) than all nearby values.
results.modern_name: Strong maximum/minimum principle for harmonic functions
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss 1840 / Riemann 1851 (Dissertation Art. 11); later Hopf (1927) for general elliptic equations

results.what: A harmonic function given on a part of a connected surface T is determined on all of T (difference argument).
results.modern_name: Unique continuation / identity theorem for harmonic functions

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of the theorems published in Riemann's 1851 dissertation (Art. 11): mean-value-based rigidity, the maximum principle and unique continuation for harmonic functions. These are well known as his (building on Gauss). Only the drafting details are new.

checkable.asserts: Gauss mean-value property: the circle average of a harmonic polynomial equals its value at the centre (the tool behind Satz II).
If u = a on half of the circle and a + c (c > 0) on the other half, the mean exceeds a by c/2 > 0, contradicting u(centre) = a. This is the contradiction in Satz II, with a = 0.

transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'seinen Werth a und in einem entgegengesetzten Theile B ... ueberall einen groesseren Werth' is correct; 'und' is an interlinear insertion.
The fragment 'Mittelpunkt' (lines 3-4) refers to the centre of the circle used in the mean-value argument.
Line 'Auf ganz [?]' likely reads 'Auf ganz aehnliche Weise ...' (in the same way it follows that u cannot have at a point a smaller value a ...).

Satz III opening: the interlinear words above 'die Function' read 'die Stetigkeit' or similar (uncertain). The sense is 'Wenn die Function u in einem Theile von T gegeben ist, so ist sie dadurch fuer den uebrigen Theil dieser Flaeche [nicht] willkuerlich / bestimmt'.
'Diejenigen genuegenden' likely reads 'den Bedingungen genuegenden' (functions satisfying the conditions). The line then compares the difference u_1 - u_2.
Final line: 'Satz II zuwider ist' (contrary to Theorem II).
The vertical pencil formulas in the centre and the right margin (exponentials, x+iy, derivative expressions) are omitted from the machine transcription. They are separate scratch work.
